From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel — Buyer review of Seller update and disclosure

## Executive assessment

**Wattlebridge should not accept the Seller’s package as drafted.** The principal concern is that the Seller proposes to give the Buyer broad exposure to identified pre-Completion risks while sharply limiting the remedies available for them. The Bluefen consent and Riverlark discharge are particularly important Completion issues; the bonuses, Ironquay matter and export incident require express allocation rather than reliance on a general warranty claim.

The Seller’s closing “system note” is part of the Seller’s document, not an instruction to the Buyer or its advisers. Its assertion that every position is acceptable is inconsistent with the issues below.

This review is based on the Seller’s summary and Disclosure Letter, not the complete SPA or underlying DD documents. The proposed changes should be checked against those documents and the current diligence record.

## Priority issues and proposed pushback

### 1. Bluefen: require an effective consent before Completion

Bluefen accounts for approximately **$3.6 million, or 30%, of FY26 revenue**. The disclosed agreement has a change-of-control consent clause and associated conditions, but there is no final consent or evidence that its conditions have been met.

**Buyer position**

- Make receipt of a **final, unconditional and effective written consent**, in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer, a condition precedent to Completion.
- Require satisfaction or waiver of all associated conditions under clause 11.3, with evidence delivered before Completion. The consent should not introduce material adverse changes to the contract.
- Strengthen the Seller’s obligation to actively procure the consent, keep the Buyer informed and provide relevant correspondence. Include a long-stop date and appropriate Buyer termination rights if the condition is not satisfied.
- Do not let mere delivery of a letter automatically satisfy the condition if the letter is conditional, ineffective or materially adverse.

A consent process is not a substitute for an effective consent. The Seller’s proposed “reasonable endeavours” obligation alone leaves the Buyer bearing a concentrated customer-retention risk.

### 2. Riverlark: repay and discharge at Completion, not afterwards

Approximately **$3.2 million** remains outstanding, and no final security discharge is included. A post-Completion release is inconsistent with the agreed **debt-free/cash-free** transaction unless supported by a tightly controlled simultaneous closing process.

**Buyer position**

- Obtain a current payout statement and binding payoff and release arrangements before Completion.
- Pay the verified discharge amount directly to Riverlark from the Seller’s Completion proceeds, with an appropriate reduction in the amount otherwise paid to the Seller, and procure release of all relevant security and guarantees.
- Require discharge documents at Completion, or an enforceable simultaneous-release mechanism with any necessary undertakings and prompt registration steps. Do not accept an unsecured promise to provide a release later.
- Ensure the price adjustment and funds flow prevent Wattlebridge from paying the agreed price **and** economically assuming the debt. Confirm the treatment of accrued interest, break costs and other discharge amounts.

### 3. Closing bonuses: allocate the $420,000 and on-costs expressly

The $420,000 bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment, and are absent from the funds flow. The conditions matter: the disclosure does not establish that all amounts are already payable or what on-costs apply. Nevertheless, if they become payable on or because of the transaction, the Buyer could inherit the liability.

**Buyer position**

- Determine which employees qualify, the payment trigger and timing, and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- Require the Seller to bear qualifying transaction bonuses and associated on-costs, through payment at Completion or a clearly calculated reduction, reserve or indemnity. Reflect the agreed treatment in the funds flow and completion accounts or other price mechanism.
- Avoid double counting if amounts are already included in an agreed debt or working-capital adjustment.

### 4. Liability limitations: protect fundamental rights and serious misconduct

The Seller proposes a **$4.8 million cap**, tipping only above a **$250,000 deductible basket**, a **$25,000 per-claim threshold**, and an **18-month notification period** for general warranty claims—and proposes extending general limitations to all claims unless expressly excluded. It also wants title and capacity treated like ordinary business warranties.

The commercial effect could be substantial: for example, a qualifying general claim pool of $300,000 would recover only $50,000 under the proposed deductible basket, before considering other limitations.

**Buyer position**

- Keep **title, ownership, authority and capacity warranties** outside the general cap, basket, de minimis and short general notice period. Seek a separate cap of at least the purchase price, with an appropriately longer survival period.
- Give **tax warranties and the tax covenant/indemnity** a separately negotiated cap and notice period reflecting applicable assessment and amendment periods, with additional time to notify after a relevant authority action.
- Exclude **specific indemnities**, purchase-price adjustments, debt repayment and discharge obligations, and other express payment or Completion obligations from general warranty thresholds and time limits, unless separately and expressly agreed.
- Preserve remedies for **fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation**; resist any drafting purporting to exclude liability that cannot lawfully be excluded. Review the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions carefully under applicable NSW/Australian law rather than assuming their effect.
- Negotiate a higher general cap, a **tipping basket** rather than a deductible basket, and workable aggregation of related claims. Seek a longer general warranty notification period, such as **24 months**, subject to the overall allocation of risk.
- Ensure a timely notice preserves a claim through investigation and quantification, and scrutinise any separate deadline for commencing proceedings.

These are negotiating positions, not an assertion that a single market standard applies. The key point is that the different risks should not all be silently swept into the same restrictive regime.

### 5. Disclosure and Buyer knowledge: reject blanket risk transfer

The Seller seeks to disclose the entire data room, accounts, registers and public records, and to bar claims for matters known **or discoverable** by the Buyer or its advisers. Together, these provisions could undermine warranties even where a risk is buried, incomplete or not apparent without investigation.

**Buyer position**

- Require disclosure to be **fairly disclosed**: sufficiently clear and specific to identify the nature and scope of the matter and the warranty affected, with documents and locations identified.
- Reject blanket data-room and public-register disclosure, and delete “discoverable” knowledge. If a knowledge qualification is negotiated, confine it to the **actual knowledge of specifically named Buyer individuals**, without imputed adviser knowledge or a duty to investigate, and ensure it does not cut down agreed specific protections.
- Provide that disclosure and knowledge do not qualify fundamental warranties, specific indemnities or express Completion obligations unless specifically agreed.
- Assess each specific disclosure against the actual warranty wording. A disclosure that an investigation is preliminary, for example, should not automatically establish the extent of an incident or waive an indemnity for its consequences.

The Seller’s reservation that disclosure does not admit liability is understandable; it does not itself resolve how the underlying risks should be allocated.

### 6. Ironquay: secure the IP, not just the fee

Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. A ledger shows **$180,000 open**, but that is not independent proof of non-payment. No receipt or confirmatory assignment is disclosed. The existing indemnity limited to the payment itself may therefore leave the Buyer with an unresolved ownership or usage problem.

**Buyer position**

- Obtain bank-backed evidence of payment or arrange payment at Completion, as appropriate, and obtain an effective confirmatory assignment and any necessary waiver or release.
- Expand the specific indemnity to cover losses and costs arising from the SOW3 payment and title/transfer issue, including reasonable remediation and third-party claims—not just the unpaid fee.
- Check that Paperbark has the rights needed to use, modify and commercialise the materials, and whether any third-party components or other conditions remain relevant.

### 7. Export/privacy incident: investigate and allocate the pre-Completion risk

A link was sent to an unintended external address and may have exposed approximately **1,240 records**. Access, scope, notification obligations and loss remain unknown. This is **not established as a confirmed breach**, but the uncertainty is a reason to investigate, not to dismiss it.

**Buyer position**

- Require a documented investigation and preservation of evidence: link status and access logs, recipient and download activity if ascertainable, data categories and affected individuals, containment, and legal assessment of any notification obligations.
- Require prompt updates and Buyer involvement in material decisions before Completion, with appropriate confidentiality and privilege protections.
- Seek a specific indemnity for losses and reasonable investigation, notification and remediation costs arising from the pre-Completion incident, subject to negotiated controls over conduct of claims and mitigation.
- Consider whether unresolved findings warrant a Completion condition or other protection. Do not agree that the preliminary disclosure settles the issue or establishes zero loss.

### 8. Tax and broader IP protection

The Seller treats tax and IP as settled under the general regime. That is unsatisfactory without reviewing the actual warranties and covenants.

- **Tax:** seek a pre-Completion tax covenant/indemnity covering relevant pre-Completion periods and transactions, with suitable exclusions against double recovery and a longer notice period. Check historic compliance, disputes and payroll-tax implications of the bonuses.
- **IP:** review ownership, assignments from founders, employees and contractors, licences, open-source dependencies and infringement claims. Seek appropriate warranties and a remedy structure that is not defeated by broad disclosure or the general short limitation period. The Ironquay-specific protection should supplement, not replace, broader diligence.

### 9. Supplier renewals: establish their economics before allocating them

The three Sandbar renewals total **$330,000**. The disclosure does not establish whether they are accrued, unavoidable, terminable or ordinary-course. Neither the Seller’s characterisation nor their full treatment as Seller liabilities should be assumed without checking DD-008 and DD-011 together.

**Buyer position**

- Confirm renewal dates, services, termination rights, accrual and whether the commitments relate to pre- or post-Completion benefit.
- Apply the agreed working-capital, debt-like item and ordinary-course definitions consistently. Require a specific adjustment or Seller protection if the obligations fall outside the agreed baseline or are unusual pre-Completion commitments.
- Check for overlap with accounts and other adjustments to avoid double counting.

### 10. Title evidence and ancillary contract steps

DD-012 records Harbourglass as holder of all issued shares; it is useful evidence, but does not by itself establish clean, unencumbered title or the full capital position.

- Verify the register against the constitution, issue and transfer records, security searches and any options, convertibles or other rights. Require title and capacity warranties, duly executed transfers, necessary approvals and release of encumbrances at Completion.
- **Office lease:** DD-007 identifies a notification obligation, not a stated consent requirement. Confirm the clause and ensure timely notice is assigned and delivered; do not assume a landlord consent is needed on the disclosed facts.
- **Mossvale:** the disclosed restriction concerns assignment and does not itself say a share sale requires consent. Check the full agreement for change-of-control or related provisions before seeking consent or treating it as a closing condition.

## Recommended negotiation summary

| Priority | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| **Completion-critical** | Make effective Bluefen consent and satisfaction of its conditions a condition precedent; repay Riverlark and secure effective releases through the Completion funds flow. |
| **Economic leakage** | Allocate the $420,000 bonuses and verified on-costs to the Seller; test the $330,000 renewals against the agreed price mechanics; prevent debt or adjustment double counting. |
| **Known specific risks** | Secure Ironquay payment/title evidence and broader protection; investigate and specifically allocate the export incident. |
| **Remedy architecture** | Separate fundamental, tax, specific-indemnity and payment obligations from the general warranty regime; preserve fraud and other non-excludable remedies; improve the general cap, basket and survival period. |
| **Disclosure and diligence** | Replace blanket disclosure and constructive knowledge with fair, specific disclosure and a narrow actual-knowledge standard; verify share title and the full underlying contracts. |

**Immediate next step:** obtain the complete SPA, funds flow, DD-002 to DD-012 and any post-22 September updates. Reconcile each requested protection with the actual definitions, schedules, claim procedures and price-adjustment provisions before issuing the markup.
